name: Penis enlargement surgery

lead: Penis enlargement surgery covers suspensory ligament release, fat injection or grafting, dermal fillers and silicone or PMMA injection, aiming for added length or girth and the body confidence that goes with it. Wikipedia states it is not medically indicated except for micropenis.

Procedures either release ligament attachments to expose more length, or add volume with fat, filler or grafts. The American Urological Association says fat injection for girth and ligament division for length have not been shown safe or efficacious, and the Sexual Medicine Society of North America issued a 2024 position statement advising against permanent fillers. A 2024 systematic review examined outcomes, complications and quality of life after penile augmentation. In looksmaxxing culture the topic is grouped under hardmaxxing.

paras: These are performed by surgeons or clinics, with recovery over weeks and sometimes post-operative stretching routines. Urology societies describe the evidence as limited and low quality.
Reported harms include scarring, shortening, deformity, infection, necrosis and erectile dysfunction. Fillers are not FDA-approved for this use, and professional bodies advise caution.

chain: Surgery or filler adds length or girth
angle.text: Surgery or filler adds penile length or girth, which men link to greater body confidence. Urology bodies describe safety and efficacy as unproven, and complications are documented in the literature.

lead: Penis enlargement surgery covers surgical and injectable procedures meant to increase penile length, girth or glans size. People who pursue it want to change how the penis looks and measures, flaccid, erect, or both. Described procedures include suspensory ligament release, fat injection or grafting, dermal fillers, silicone or PMMA injection, graft-based girth surgery and, in specialist centres, flap, sleeve and lengthening techniques.[1][2]

In medicine the topic sits between reconstructive urology and cosmetic surgery. Surgical enlargement is accepted mainly for micropenis, where it can improve urinary or sexual function as well as size.[1][3] Professional bodies describe cosmetic enlargement as poorly standardised: the American Urological Association (AUA) has held since 1994 that fat injection for girth and ligament division for length have not been shown safe or efficacious, the Sexual Medicine Society of North America (SMSNA) issued position statements in 2024 on five invasive cosmetic procedures, and the Fifth International Consultation on Sexual Medicine (ICSM 2024) produced twenty graded recommendations.[1][4][5]

Body image is part of the discussion. Some doctors say many men who seek enlargement have normal-sized penises and may underestimate their own size or overestimate the average, and reference studies of measured size are used in counselling.[1][6][7][2] In looksmaxxing culture the topic is grouped under hardmaxxing, the surgical end of appearance change, and sits beside non-surgical practices such as traction, pumps and jelqing that are covered as separate topics.

paras: Wikipedia defines penis enlargement as any technique aimed at increasing penile size, whether total length, shaft girth, or the size of the glans and foreskin; surgery is one group alongside supplements, pumps, jelqing and traction.[1] Surgical methods are the ones with the clearest physical effect on measured size, and they are also the ones professional societies address most directly.[1][4]

The 2024 ICSM consultation frames the field in terms of what a procedure changes: some techniques raise flaccid or erect length, others add to shaft girth or glans size. It lists exercises, traction devices and medical therapy as non-surgical strategies, and cosmetic and phallic reconstructive techniques using fillers, sleeves, grafts and flaps as surgical ones.[4]

Suspensory ligament release divides the ligament that anchors the penis to the pubic bone. It increases flaccid length because more of the shaft projects outward, but it does not increase erect length and can affect sexual function.[1] The AUA considers division of the suspensory ligament for lengthening in adults a procedure not shown to be safe or efficacious, and the SMSNA addressed ligament division as one of its five procedure categories.[1][5]

Fat transfer harvests fat from elsewhere in the body and injects or grafts it onto the penis to add girth. Wikipedia reports that grafted fat can be effective but the gain may fade over time, and that fat injection can cause swelling and deformity, in some cases needing removal of tissue.[1] The AUA position on subcutaneous fat injection for girth has stood since January 1994.[1]

Injectable fillers include hyaluronic acid, polylactic acid, silicone gel and PMMA. Hyaluronic acid and polylactic acid have shown limited efficacy, dermal fillers are not FDA-approved for the penis, and the SMSNA strongly recommends against permanent fillers such as paraffin and silicone.[1] The SMSNA 2024 statements include injectable soft tissue fillers as one of the five categories reviewed.[5]

subs.h: Grafts, flaps, sleeves and lengthening techniques
paras: An Italian series from 1995 to 1997 described albugineal surgery with bilateral saphenous vein grafts to increase the girth of the erect penis in 39 patients who requested more diameter.[8] The 2024 systematic review in Medicina divided techniques by aim: those changing perceived length (lipoplasty, skin reconstruction, V-Y and Z plasty, flap reconstruction, scrotoplasty, ventral phalloplasty, ligament release), those changing actual corporal length (penile disassembly, total phalloplasty, sliding elongation) and those adding girth (soft tissue fillers, grafting, biodegradable scaffolds and the Penuma device).[5] The SMSNA statements also cover graft-and-flap procedures, silicone sleeve implants and sliding techniques.[5]
A 2008 review of penile size and enlargement discussed lengthening, girth enhancement and skin reconstruction procedures with their indications and complications.[9]

Surgical enlargement is accepted in medical practice mainly for micropenis, which Wikipedia defines by a length at least 2.5 standard deviations below the mean for age and which usually arises from reduced prenatal androgen action. Surgical methods developed for enlargement have been applied to micropenis but have not achieved wide acceptance because outcomes are not reliably successful.[3] Hormone treatment is the usual first step in infancy; a 1987 Journal of Urology study gave parenteral testosterone before reconstructive surgery in 44 patients with hypospadias, epispadias or urethral fistulas, as a separate paediatric indication.[10]

Penile lengthening is also being studied in men undergoing penile prosthesis implantation for erectile dysfunction; a registered trial of lengthening before prosthesis implantation began recruiting in August 2025 with a planned 48 participants.[11]

Penile size is a major concern for many men, according to reference studies whose authors say their data are meant to help counsel patients worried about size or seeking surgery.[6][7] Measured averages vary by population: a study of 301 Indian men reported a mean flaccid length of 8.21 cm and a mean erect length of 13.01 cm in the 93 men measured erect, while a study of 5,196 Chinese men reported a mean flaccid length of 6.5 cm, stretched length 12.9 cm, and erect length 12.9 cm in a subgroup of 311.[6][7]

Some doctors say that most men who seek enlargement have penises within the normal range and may have penile dysmorphophobia, and a 2006 paper by Vardi questioned the ethics of operating on such men.[1][2] Body dysmorphic disorder, first described by Enrico Morselli in 1886 as dysmorphophobia, can focus on any body part; Wikipedia notes that people with it who pursue cosmetic surgery often do not find relief, that cosmetic surgeons and psychiatrists are encouraged to screen patients together, and that a Penile Dysmorphic Disorder screening scale has been published.[12] The 2024 Medicina review concluded that augmentation surgery may help men troubled by genital size but that risks and complexity must be weighed, and that treatment should be tailored to each man's history and psychological state.[5]

A 2008 review noted that long-term data and patient-rated satisfaction were lacking in many studies. A 2019 review in Sexual Medicine Reviews, summarised by Wikipedia, described outcomes as poor with low satisfaction rates and evidence as scant and low quality; its authors argued that injectables and surgery should be a last option and unethical outside clinical trials.[1]

The 2024 Medicina systematic review searched PubMed and Scopus in December 2023, retrieved 1,670 articles and included 46, measuring length, girth, complications and quality of life; its abstract does not give pooled gain or satisfaction figures.[5] The SMSNA statements are expert consensus based on a literature review through December 2023, and the authors list reliance on expert opinion and limited research as limitations.[5] The ICSM conclusion stresses that long-term data are limited and that thorough assessment and counselling are essential before treatment.[4]

Reported complications include scarring that may lead to shortening or erectile dysfunction, deformity, infection and necrosis, and in some cases removal of tissue.[1] Procedures by unlicensed operators have caused serious harm: in 2013, many Vietnamese men injected liquid silicone and were hospitalised with infections, necrosis, tumours, swelling, deformities and sexual dysfunction.[1] A 1997 Journal of Urology paper described how deformities resulting from enlargement surgery were reconstructed.[13]

Guidance documents ask for experienced surgeons and individualised choices. The ICSM conclusion says surgical decisions should reflect the patient's condition and needs, the surgeon's expertise and local resources.[4]

The AUA and the Urology Care Foundation have held since January 1994 that fat injection for girth and ligament division for length have not been shown to be safe or efficacious, and have reaffirmed this since.[1] Dermal fillers are not FDA-approved for penile use.[1] In April 2024 the SMSNA published its position statement on cosmetic penile enhancement in the Journal of Sexual Medicine, with six statements for five procedure categories.[5] The ICSM 2024 document followed with twenty new recommendations, each with a level of evidence and grade.[4]

Preclinical work includes a 2024 study of a polyvinyl alcohol hydrogel patch with a negative Poisson's ratio structure, designed to conform to penile deformation; in rabbits it enlarged the penis without degradation or fibrosis.[14] The registered prosthesis-lengthening trial is a clinical example.[11]

Studies are mostly surgical case series and reviews. The Italian albugineal series (1995-1997, 39 patients) aimed to give a real increase in erect size using saphenous vein grafts.[8] The 2024 Medicina systematic review summarised outcomes, complications and quality of life after augmentation techniques across 46 included studies.[5] The SMSNA position statement gave recommendations for injection and surgical procedures and for future research,[5] and the ICSM 2024 guideline gave twenty graded recommendations.[4] A registered trial is examining penile lengthening before penile prosthesis implantation.[11] Preclinical work includes the 2024 hydrogel patch study in rabbits.[14]

Products promising enlargement were heavily advertised by spam email in the late 1990s and early 2000s. Wikipedia notes a leaked 2003 log showing about 6,000 orders for one herbal product in four weeks, and the US Federal Trade Commission said that there was no proof the pills worked as advertised.[1] Wikipedia also covers non-surgical methods, including pumps, jelqing and traction, as separate topics; it reports that evidence for traction is mixed, that clinical trials have not found pumps effective for enlargement, and that jelqing has no medical evidence and has been linked to fibrosis.[1]

In looksmaxxing vocabulary, enlargement surgery belongs to hardmaxxing, the group of surgical and invasive changes. Forum discussion of size also appears in general fitness communities; T Nation posts mention both the insecurity around size and the perceived lengthening that some men notice after losing fat around the pubic area.[15][16]

lore.intro: Claims about enlargement surgery are made by clinics, patients and forum users; professional societies and reviewers respond with their own positions.
